findings.text: the gate table caption cites logs/baseline/ and logs/after/ as the two arms, but logs/after/ does not exist and logs/baseline/ holds five of the six files with baseline-test_media.log truncated before its summary and EXIT line, so the counts cannot be checked from the paths the record names; line 36's 'every log's last line is a bare EXIT=0' is also false for that file. The counts do reconcile with the combined logs/baseline-suite.log and logs/after-suite.log that the manifest cites.

the base arm's header names the imported module as /home/ITER/mcintos/Code/nova/nova/__init__.py, the main checkout, while naming 6c642019 as its revision and the node worktree as its tree; the log therefore cannot show which tree the base arm imported. The measurement is sound in substance because nova code is identical between 6c642019 and the main head b1c42788e (the delta is docs only), but the header is not the provenance it claims.

reclaim_legacy_group duplicates the zarr group-deletion mechanism owned by ZarrStore.delete_group at nova/database/zarrstore.py:148-155 (open mode 'a' then del root[name]) rather than extending that owner to take a group name, so two places now know how to remove a group from a store.

VERDICT done_when: the done_when asks for a one-group re-ingest test with the removal reported, a replaceable self-fulfilling assertion, and six covering files by delta in fresh processes; tests/test_signalstore_convention_key.py:129-151 asserts stored_groups(fresh) == {fresh.cache_key} plus the printed legacy name, and logs/after-suite.log records 93 passed against logs/baseline-suite.log's 92, both EXIT=0.
